_purpose: Cross-skill description-optimization / collision check across all 5 FTC skills together (5th skill, ftc-construct, added §22 post-Session-2). 23 queries: should-route-to-one-skill (with the expected owner), should-not-cleanly-route or are deliberately ambiguous near-misses. Includes the three REQUIRED tight-boundary pairs (A: HW specs vs RC allowed; B: TC vs CR on an intentless repo look; C — NEW: TC vs CO on generation-adjacent phrasing). This is the check that can only run with all 5 assembled — collision is invisible testing a skill alone.

queries.query: we're a rookie team on the goBILDA strafer kit, mecanum, one control hub — set up our robot config and write a basic teleop so we can drive
queries.why: codegen request with no confirmed config -> TC before generation

queries.query: what's the free speed of a goBILDA 5203 at 19.2:1, and how many encoder ticks per rev for odometry?
queries.why: spec + math

queries.query: our robot is 19 inches wide sitting on the field before the match — are we going to fail inspection?
queries.why: legality/inspection

queries.query: our flywheel shooter behaves differently every match for no reason and we already swapped the motor — can you look at the code?
queries.why: 'behaves differently for no reason' hardware-flake-looking symptom -> CR corpus catch

queries.query: what are the specs on the REV 12V slim battery — capacity in mAh and the connector type?
queries.why: TIGHT PAIR A (specs side): a spec lookup, not a legality question -> HW

queries.query: which batteries are we actually allowed to run at competition this season?
queries.why: TIGHT PAIR A (allowed side): legality of a part -> RC, resolves Table 12-4 by pointer into HW

queries.query: can you do a full pre-competition review of our whole TeamCode before this weekend?
queries.why: whole-codebase pre-comp review -> CR full-review

queries.query: we bolted on a single-axis turret this week — write the aiming subsystem for it
queries.why: mid-season mechanism change before codegen -> TC re-elicits then generates

queries.query: how far is our arm allowed to extend past the 18-inch starting cube once the match is running?
queries.why: expansion-limit rules

queries.query: what gear ratio do I need to lift a 2 kg arm on a 5203, and will it hold position?
queries.why: torque/ratio math

queries.query: what's the weather forecast in Houston for the world championship next month?
queries.why: irrelevant near-miss (FTC-event context, no skill)

queries.query: write me a python script that scrapes the FTC-Events API for our division's current rankings
queries.why: near-miss: FTC + code, but it's tooling not robot-code review/config/rules/hardware

queries.query: what's team 14584's OPR right now?
queries.why: R65 deferred (FTCScout live data) -> abstain, no skill owns it yet

queries.query: our robot keeps dropping its wifi connection to the driver station mid-match, how do we fix it?
queries.why: networking/IT near-miss, not covered by any skill

queries.query: should we play offense or defense against the number-1 seed in our next elim match?
queries.why: match strategy near-miss (not rules/hardware/config/review)

queries.query: we're brand new this year — what should our first robot even look like?
queries.why: R78 explicitly-deferred gap: from-scratch design advice owned by no skill this pass

queries.query: hey can you take a look at our repo?
queries.why: TIGHT PAIR B: 'look at our repo' with no intent -> genuinely spans TC (infer/confirm config) and CR (review). Testing that descriptions don't hard-collide; a reasonable clarify-or-pick is acceptable, a confident wrong lock-in is not

queries.query: translate the comments in our autonomous opmode into Spanish for our sister team
queries.why: near-miss: touches robot code but it's translation, not review/config

queries.query: conceptually what's the difference between mecanum and swerve drive?
queries.why: general-knowledge near-miss; not a spec lookup, config, rule, or review action

queries.query: how much does a goBILDA 5203 motor cost these days?
queries.why: HW boundary near-miss: price is NOT a catalog spec -> HW should abstain, not a spec lookup it owns

queries.query: write me a teleop OpMode for our shooter
queries.why: the exact §23 boundary-test phrase: pure generation request, no config-setup or config-change language attached -> CO. CO's own precondition (R82) hands back to TC if no config is confirmed yet -- routing here tests the FIRST hop, not the full turn

queries.query: generate the ShooterOpMode.java for us
queries.why: pure generation request, same class as q21

queries.query: add an intake subsystem
queries.why: TIGHT PAIR C (NEW, §23): near-identical phrasing appears in BOTH descriptions on purpose ('add an intake' in TC's, 'add an intake subsystem' in CO's) -- accepted overlap, not a defect, per the same standard q17 already set for TC/CR. Passes if either owner is picked AND that owner's own body correctly hands off/back rather than guessing; fails only on a confident wrong THIRD skill or no plausible owner at all.

result_4_skill_original.note: Historical record from the original Session-2 assembly pass, BEFORE ftc-construct (§22) existed. Queries 1-20, 4 skills only. Superseded by result_5_skill_rerun below for anything involving codegen routing.
result_4_skill_original.tight_pair_B_look_at_repo: q17 resolved to ftc-code-review (not a hard collision); acceptable — CR's body hands back to ftc-team-config if config is missing/wrong, so CR-first is safe. Genuine ambiguity resolved to a valid single owner.
result_4_skill_original.negatives: all 10 NONE correct, incl. the tricky ones: motor PRICE did NOT over-trigger HW (q20), from-scratch design did NOT over-trigger TC (q16), python scraper did NOT trigger CR (q12)
result_4_skill_original.verdict: No description changes needed. Descriptions are well-differentiated: 0 collisions, 0 under-triggers on should-trigger queries, 0 negative over-triggers.

result_5_skill_rerun.method: Fresh general-purpose agent, zero prior context, given ONLY the 5 skills' exact frontmatter descriptions plus the 23 queries stripped of expected/why fields — same blind methodology as the original 4-skill run.
result_5_skill_rerun.boundary_test_result_the_user_asked_for: PASS. q21 ('write me a teleop OpMode for our shooter') and q22 ('generate the ShooterOpMode.java for us') both routed cleanly to ftc-construct with no hedging — the bare-generation-request case the user's Step 5 explicitly named. q23 ('add an intake subsystem', TIGHT PAIR C) resolved as AMBIGUOUS:ftc-team-config|ftc-construct exactly as designed — accepted per the same standard q17 already set, since either owner's body correctly hands off/back (TC hands to CO once confirmed; CO hands back to TC if unconfirmed — see R82, live-tested separately below in the runbook, not just described). q1 and q8 (config-setup / mid-season-change language) still correctly resolved to ftc-team-config, NOT ftc-construct — confirms construct's overlapping example phrasing does not over-trigger when the query carries config-establishing context.
result_5_skill_rerun.handback_mechanism_live_test: Ran `python3 .claude/skills/ftc-team-config/scripts/validate_config.py .claude/skills/ftc-team-config/evals/fixtures/rookie-mecanum-stock.yaml` directly (real script, real fixture with an unconfirmed mandatory field) — returned `generation_allowed: false, unconfirmed_mandatory: ["software_stack.pathing"]`. This is the exact signal ftc-construct's §0 precondition checks before generating; confirms the mechanism CO's handback depends on already works correctly. Separately discovered and fixed: validate_config.py raises an unhandled traceback (not a clean result) when the config file doesn't exist at all rather than being merely unconfirmed — ftc-construct's §0 was written to check file existence with a plain check FIRST, before ever invoking the script, to avoid depending on the script handling that case (it doesn't).

incidental_findings_pre_existing_not_int.text: which batteries are we actually allowed to run at competition this season?
incidental_findings_pre_existing_not_int.finding: This blind run flagged AMBIGUOUS:ftc-hardware-lookup|ftc-rule-check where the original run cleanly split q5->HW/q6->RC. Root cause is pre-existing and unrelated to §22: ftc-hardware-lookup's own description names 'the game manual's legal-parts tables' as its own remit, which genuinely overlaps ftc-rule-check's 'whether a... part... is allowed' framing. Not caused by adding ftc-construct; flagged here because this re-run is what surfaced it. Out of scope for §22 to fix — noted, not silently dropped, matching this project's own deferred-not-silent convention.

incidental_findings_pre_existing_not_int.text: our robot keeps dropping its wifi connection to the driver station mid-match, how do we fix it?
incidental_findings_pre_existing_not_int.finding: This blind run over-triggered ftc-code-review (reasoning: 'hardware-flake-looking symptoms are often code-structure problems', quoted from CR's own description) on what the original test scored as a clean NONE (pure networking/IT near-miss). Pre-existing breadth in CR's description, unrelated to §22. Noted, not fixed this pass — a future CR description tightening pass could narrow 'hardware-flake-looking' to exclude pure connectivity/networking symptoms.

result_5_skill_rerun.verdict: The §22-specific boundary test PASSES cleanly: ftc-construct is reachable via a bare generation request, correctly excluded when config-establishing context is present, and its deliberate overlap with ftc-team-config resolves the same safe way the pre-existing TC/CR tight pair already does. Two unrelated, pre-existing description-softness findings surfaced incidentally (q6, q14) — fixed, see result_post_fix_reverify below.

result_post_fix_reverify.note: HW's and CR's descriptions were tightened to fix q6 and q14 (see SKILL.md diffs — HW now explicitly carves out legality-verdict phrasing to RC; CR now explicitly excludes pure connectivity/networking symptoms). Re-ran the full blind classifier fresh (new agent, zero prior context) against the updated descriptions to confirm.
result_post_fix_reverify.q6_battery_legality: FIXED, confirmed — classifier now resolves cleanly to ftc-rule-check, explicitly citing HW's new carve-out text. No longer ambiguous.
result_post_fix_reverify.q14_wifi_networking: FIXED, confirmed — classifier now resolves to NONE, explicitly citing CR's new exclusion text. No longer over-triggers ftc-code-review.
result_post_fix_reverify.new_observation_not_a_defect: This re-run's classifier resolved the bare generation queries (q21 'write me a teleop OpMode for our shooter', q22 'generate the ShooterOpMode.java for us', q23 'add an intake subsystem') to ftc-team-config rather than ftc-construct — different from the PRIOR blind run, which picked ftc-construct for q21/q22 and AMBIGUOUS for q23. The agent itself flagged why: a stateless classifier with no repo context cannot know whether a team-config.yaml already exists and is confirmed, so it defaults conservatively to ftc-team-config (a reasonable default under uncertainty, not a bug) — construct's own precondition (R82) is designed to be checked WITH real session/repo state, which a bare-string classification test cannot simulate. This is a known limitation of the stateless-classifier proxy, not of the actual routing mechanism: the real, session-aware behavior (does TC correctly recognize an ALREADY-confirmed config on disk and hand off to construct) was independently validated by the trimmed TC re-eval's scenario 3 (rookie/veteran fixtures, real validate_config.py run, real hand-off transcript) — see evals/post-construct-split-reeval.md. Both runs of the stateless test are defensible; neither represents a routing collision or a wrong-skill lock-in.
result_post_fix_reverify.verdict: Both incidental findings confirmed fixed with no new collisions introduced. The construct-reachability question is better answered by the session-aware re-eval than by a stateless classifier, and that re-eval already passed.
